profile.headline: Lead AI Software Engineer
profile.summary:
I build AI systems for biomedical researchers. Right now that means leading the engineering for generative AI solutions in Mayo Clinic's research organization, platforms that help scientists find data, navigate policy and procedure, and connect with the right collaborators.

I came to this from the bench. I started in ophthalmology research, running lab experiments and analysis on corneal disease, LASIK, and transplant. From there I moved into software for proteomics analysis, then data warehousing for health policy research, then a decade of building clinical laboratory applications for Mayo's Clinical Genomics program alongside genetic counselors and geneticists. The science background is not a footnote. Knowing how a lab actually works, and how a researcher or clinician actually thinks, is the difference between an AI tool people demo once and one they use every day.

My work now spans four areas:

Architecture. Designing generative AI systems on Google Cloud, using Vertex AI, Cloud Run, BigQuery, and Terraform: agentic systems, retrieval over research data and institutional knowledge, and the infrastructure to evaluate all of it.

Design. Working directly with researchers to shape interfaces and workflows, the same stakeholder-first approach I used building genomics tools for the last ten years.

Engineering. Hands on with Python, FastAPI, LangGraph, PyTorch, RAG, fine tuning, Model Context Protocol, and LLM evaluation with DeepEval. I still write code and I still read the PRs.

Product management. I hold a Master of Science in Project Management and trained others in agile practice across the institution. I set priorities with stakeholders and keep a fast-moving effort pointed at real research outcomes.

I am a ferocious learner, educator, and builder. I present in enterprise developer forums, attend grand rounds in individualized medicine, and stay active in institutional workgroups. The technology under me keeps changing. That is the part I like.

positions.title: Lead Software Engineer
positions.description: A Leading engineering for Mayo's Research Data Atlas (formerly Omics Data Platform) team since 2022, a role that keeps shifting under me as the underlying technology does. I've moved from core data platform work on GCP into building AI/ML tooling and generative AI systems for the broader research organization, most recently leading Research Atlas AI Services and architecting Atlas Navigator, an institutional AI platform for Mayo researchers. It's a good role for an engineer who wants to lead through rapid changes in responsibility and tech stack rather than settle into one lane. I'm a ferocious learner, educator, and builder, and this job keeps testing all three.

projects.title: Atlas Navigator
projects.description:
Lead Engineer & Architect. Led architecture and technical direction for Atlas Navigator, an institutional AI platform that helps Mayo Clinic researchers discover and access research resources, data, and support services through a conversational interface.

- Designed a multi-agent system on LangGraph and Vertex AI Gemini, spanning six agent surfaces: grounded FAQ chat with natural-language BigQuery data discovery, IRB study-drafting assistance, researcher profile building, an admin corpus-management assistant, and request intake/drafting tools.
- Architected the platform on Google Cloud (Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, BigQuery, GCS) behind an Identity-Aware Proxy/SSO boundary, with strict data-governance controls (no protected health information reaches the LLM layer).
- Delivered a 4-week proof of concept that validated the platform's two headline capabilities, earning executive approval to advance into full product development.
- Established architecture decision records and alignment with the organization's shared agent-platform reference architecture to guide the team through sustained development.

projects.title: TeamFabric
projects.description: Built and maintain TeamFabric, an open-source, file-based working memory system for software teams operated by an AI agent. Teams drop in raw content (meeting notes, standups, decisions) and the agent organizes it into structured, queryable entities. Includes modules for backlog refinement, request triage, standups, and retrospectives, plus a command and skill system built on Claude Code. MIT licensed.
